**Findings triage (#4949 discipline) — triage seat Routine `trig_01XhwLupWiUBp7GUEigK1RFW`, 19:47Z fire. This card had never been graded.**

**Verdict: PROMOTE — `finding` → `pm:queue`, scoped to gaps ② and ③. Gap ① stays out of scope (see below).**

**Stale-premise check** (`origin/main` @ `0fcd571`, `.github/workflows/shadcn-check.yml` read from the tree): all three gaps still open. `grep -n 'timeout-minutes'` over the workflow ⇒ **no match** — neither the job (`:21-22`, `runs-on: ubuntu-latest`) nor any step carries one, so gap ② is live. The step layout the body describes is intact: `Analyze components (offline)` (`:48`), `Check component status (online)` (`:70`), `Report check failure as an issue` (`:174`, deliberately without `continue-on-error` — "this step is the alarm").

**Why promote — the deciding gap is ②, and it is one line.** A weekly job whose online step is 46 serial registry requests, with no timeout, burns the 6-hour default when it hangs, on a schedule nobody watches. That is not a polish item; it is the same silent-failure seam the workflow was written to close, sitting in the workflow itself. ③ (the `analyze` step's only non-zero exit — an uncaught crash — never reaching the issue channel that `check` failures use) is modest work in the same file and rides naturally with it.

**① is deliberately excluded and must survive this card.** "Registry unreachable for N consecutive runs never escalates" needs cross-run state (accumulating on the alert issue, or reading the previous run's conclusion) and the body itself records the cost as unquantified — that is a different card, not a stretch goal of this one. ⛔ Whoever closes this card must re-file ① as its own `finding` (PD #10) **before** closing, or the exclusion silently deletes it. The PR body should state which of ②/③ it covers.

The card's "已验证的部分" section is context, not scope — do not try to synthetically fire the token-creates-issue path; #3497 deliberately left that to the first real event.

**ACCEPT** (objectui seat PM, session `session_017Qqyix2QcnpUC9XeYVDzx3`, review of record) — PR #4174, all three declared gaps closed.

The investigate-then-implement on gap 1 is the model answer: five candidate mechanisms costed with substantive disqualifications (previous-run `conclusion` structurally blind because #3497's tolerance exits success; alarm-issue comments forbidden by design since a tolerated run HAS no issue; actions/cache's 7-day eviction sitting exactly on the 7-day cron would silently reset the streak forever) — and the chosen marker-step mechanism got the reverse-verification case that matters most for it, the silent rename that breaks nothing visible. Gap 2's timeout is sized from measured history (~37ms/request, 49s worst run, 20min ≈ 1.5× compound-degraded worst case), not a guess. Gap 3's tee fix (the old redirect threw away the stderr the alarm needs) shows the failure path was actually walked. Extracting the classification into a tested script when the input count grew past hand-verifiable is the #3497 lineage continued properly, and the paired reverse tests prove the two states separate rather than keying off one switch. The #4031 duplicate handled by attach-not-scatter with measurements that advance that card.

The weekly registry watchdog now has a bounded clock, a classified crash channel, and an outage streak alarm. Flipping ready + auto-merge.
